thread:
Anna K: Heads up — we're seeing a surge in preemptible GPU interruptions in us-central1 over the last 18h. Pod restarts up ~4x, queueing for long-running batch jobs.
Rafael M: saw the alert. Any correlation with recent instance image or kernel update?
Anna K: No kernel/image changes in infra. I checked cloud events — lots of preemption notices and rapid instance churn.
Jordan S: Confirmed. Streaming logs: 
```
2026-03-17T04:12:03Z PREEMPTIBLE_TERMINATION NOTICE instance-id=xyz zone=us-central1-a
2026-03-17T04:12:11Z GCE: Preempting instance xyz (gpu-nvidia-rtx4090)
```
Priya V: This is the third regional blip this quarter. Last time we fell back to on-demand pool which spiked cost by ~60% for the day.
Ben C: Cost hit sucked but customers didn't see errors because fallback worked. But the autoscaler struggled: pod boot time + node provisioning created a backlog.
Anna K: Reproducible pattern: preemptible pool drains -> cluster-autoscaler scales up on-demand fallback -> long scheduling due to GPU taints/tolerations and image pull for large model artifacts.
Rafael M: Current node pool config for preemptible: taint: `preemptible=true:NoSchedule`, nodeSelector: `gpu-type:rtx4090`, autoscaler profiles: `min=0 max=50` (preemptible), fallback pool `min=5 max=100 on-demand`.
Jordan S: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) increase fallback pool min from 5->15 for next 24h 2) enable faster node provisioning by pre-baking GPU image (smaller layers) 3) add soft-eviction hook to requeue long-running jobs to a spot-aware job queue.
Priya V: Agree but increasing fallback min will burn credits. We need an estimate. Last fallback day cost delta: $12k. If we bump to min15 we estimate ~$3.8k/day.
Ben C: Alternative short term: reduce pod disruption budget for batch jobs to allow quicker evictions and faster scheduling on remaining nodes. Could trade throughput for recovery speed.
Anna K: Can we do a mixed strategy: bump fallback min to 10, bake images, and enable aggressive node-provisioning template?
Rafael M: Yep. Also want to try a new CA (cluster-autoscaler) flag: `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` and `--max-empty-bulk-delete=10` to speed reclaim/scale decisions.
Jordan S: Also propose tagging preemptible nodes with a label `recently-preempted=true` and route new pods away from those zones for 10m via affinity rules while drain completes. Might reduce thrash.
Priya V: That might help. How invasive is adding that label + routing?
Ben C: Simple controller (10 LOC) that watches terminations and labels nodes. We'll add tolerations for system pods only.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-4321 — preemptible churn us-central1 — severity: medium — https://internal.incidents/INC-20260317-4321
Anna K: Plan for next 6 hours:
- (immediate) increase fallback pool min to 10 (Rafael)
- (30m) start baking slim GPU image and push to gcr (Jordan + Ben)
- (1h) deploy node-labeler controller and CA flag changes to staging then canary (Rafael)
- (3h) monitor queue length and pod Pending time, revert if cost > $6k above baseline (Priya)
Rafael M: I'll open the infra PR with the autoscaler flags + pool change: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/6a1b2c3 (will tag for rollback).
Jordan S: Image bake started: `gcloud builds submit --tag gcr.io/redwood/gpu-slim:20260317-01`
Ben C: Node-labeler snippet (will add to PR):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: node-labeler
spec:
  containers:
  - name: labeler
    image: gcr.io/redwood/node-labeler:latest
    args: ["--watch-preemptions", "--label=recently-preempted=true", "--ttl=600"]
```
Priya V: Please post cost delta estimate in the PR and add an alert rule `preemptible.fallback.cost > 5000` to paging channel.
Anna K: Agreed. Also add a dashboard panel: `Cluster pending pods by GPU type` and `Average pod startup latency (GPU)` — link to dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/clusters/gpu-overview
Rafael M: PR up: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1423 — includes pool min -> 10, CA flags, and node-labeler deployment. Rolling canary to us-central1-b first.
Jordan S: Canary started. Watching metrics: Pending pods down ~30% in first 8 minutes.
Ben C: +1 on the labeler doing its thing — nodes in us-central1-a got `recently-preempted=true` and scheduler routed jobs to us-central1-b/c.
Priya V: Initial cost projection if canary holds: +$1.9k/day. Acceptable for 48h while we stabilize.
Anna K: Good. After 24-48h we'll evaluate: if preemptions persistent, we need longer-term options: dedicated reserved pools for critical workloads or region failover automation.
Rafael M: We'll keep autoscaler conservative on teardown to avoid oscillations. Will post a short retrospective with metrics.
Jordan S: If anyone sees customer impact or spikes in tail latency, ping #support immediately.
Ben C: thumbs: :thumbsup:
Anna K: Thanks everyone. Closing thread once PR merges and canary green.
infra-bot: PR merged: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1423 — deployed to us-central1-b canary
Anna K: Canary green after 2h. Marking resolved for now.
Rafael M: Will open follow-up to test region failover playbook in staging.
Priya V: Will monitor cost and report back Monday.
Ben C: nice work.
Anna K: Resolving — thanks all :tada:
